recommended_title: Score-Targeted Subsets for Predicting LLM Benchmark Accuracy
central_question: How accurately can a source-trained, score-targeted shared item subset and decoder predict retained full-benchmark accuracy and model rankings at 5-, 10-, and 25-item budgets, relative to local benchmark-estimation baselines, and where does the comparison reverse?
central_thesis: On nine frozen benchmark matrices, the evaluated score-targeted acquisition-and-decoding package has lower average accuracy-prediction error than the recorded baselines when averaging equally over benchmarks, seeds, and query budgets, but its advantage over local IRT is not uniform across benchmarks and does not establish the benefit of any individual decoder component or transfer beyond this snapshot.
narrative_rationale: The strongest evidence is the completed final evaluation of one frozen package against paired, budget-matched local estimators, including an evaluator-provided lineage-block uncertainty analysis. The independent qualification sources report completed and qualified; no downstream_study is present. Aggregate candidate MAE is 0.038991605535293065, compared with local IRT 0.05911223215296765 and uniform sampling 0.10520541810011626. The IRT paired MAE-difference interval excludes zero conditional on the fixed cases, while the raw case-by-budget predictions reveal reversals in math, legalbench, and med_qa. These reversals are part of the thesis, not inconvenient supplementary-only results. Prefer one shared estimation question with condition-specific evidence blocks for the leaderboard and HELM matrices, not separate chronological experiments. Reject a random-audit unbiasedness paper because that is not the final evaluated package; reject a nonlinear-decoder superiority paper because activation and isolated component effects are unverified; reject a universal or adaptive-evaluation story because the evaluated item path is source-only and shared across targets. The empirical framing is ready, but the supplied bibliography needs task-relevant, permitted-source repair before a defensible final related-work section can be written.

Diagnostic postprocessing of final raw predictions, excluding replay and using lineage-equal weights, identifies local IRT reversals: math at all budgets, legalbench at 5 and 25, and med_qa at 10 and 25. These derived diagnostic signs determine the main figure plan; exact plotted values must be regenerated from the same records, not copied from rounded diagnostics.

method_groups.name: Score-targeted acquisition and source-selected score decoding
method_groups.include_reason: This is the frozen final package: lineage-weighted source response/score covariance, regularized conditional-gain selection with one representative per content group, a nested common subset, and all-observation decoding. Explain linear ridge/offset and optional log-odds plus residual ridge as implemented alternatives within the package; do not claim the optional branch was active or responsible for the measured gain.

method_groups.name: Uniform content-group sampling
method_groups.include_reason: Recorded, budget-matched simple comparator. The local implementation samples distinct content-group representatives, accounts for group mass, and clips its estimate; describe this rather than silently substituting an ordinary unweighted item mean.

method_groups.name: Source-score prior
method_groups.include_reason: Recorded no-target-response reference quantifies what can be predicted from source scores alone; its observation cost is zero even when displayed beside the other methods at each budget.

method_groups.name: Response-vector anchors
method_groups.include_reason: Recorded source-response representative selection and cluster-weighted averaging contextualize a structurally different acquisition/estimation family. The local normalized-response, farthest-first implementation is not an attested reproduction of the published Anchor Points method.

method_groups.name: Local Rasch-style IRT estimator
method_groups.include_reason: The strongest recorded aggregate comparator and the essential reference for heterogeneous failures. It uses source-fitted item difficulty, the same uniform query path as the uniform baseline, and queried-response target-ability fitting. It is not the complete tinyBenchmarks system or an exhaustive tuned IRT comparison.

results_focus: Primary estimand: full mean binary accuracy over the retained, reconciled item matrix, not necessarily the original unfiltered benchmark. Primary error is target-lineage-equal MAE, then equally averaged across the declared budgets, seeds, and nine cases. Source and target model-lineage group assignments are disjoint under the supplied metadata policy, not under a proved complete ancestry relation.

Main aggregate table: selected package MAE 0.038991605535293065 and RMSE 0.04837892636321264; local IRT MAE 0.05911223215296765; uniform 0.10520541810011626; source prior 0.08335016635136305; anchors 0.15674229873896958. Ground every reported final metric in final.metric.* and keep raw score units in [0,1]. Do not imply these averages are specifically 25-item results.

Main paired uncertainty view: candidate-minus-IRT MAE -0.02012062661767458, recorded 95% interval [-0.02570984836073398, -0.014632649205711504]. Also show the recorded paired differences and intervals against uniform, prior, and anchors. The 200-draw lineage-block bootstrap retains seeds and budgets within groups and conditions on the fixed nine cases; the identical interval repeated in each seed wrapper is one aggregate analysis, not three independent intervals.

Main heterogeneity view: all nine cases at each budget, expressed as paired candidate-minus-local-IRT MAE with a common zero reference. Preserve math losses at every budget, legalbench reversals at 5 and 25, and med_qa reversals at 10 and 25. Do not infer causes from ecosystem membership, source count, or benchmark names. Any case-specific interval would require a documented new postprocessing analysis; the supplied aggregate interval cannot be reused as a per-case interval.

Ranking is a distinct outcome, not an inferred consequence of MAE: final Spearman 0.8158480130897703 and Kendall 0.6715966634525837 are calculated on lineage-mean predictions/truth and then averaged by the evaluator. Do not concatenate models from different benchmarks into one correlation. Baseline ranking cells may be filled only by a reproducible extraction from existing baseline predictions with exactly the same rules; otherwise show not reported, not zero, and make no ranking-superiority claim.

Robustness/control reporting: recorded permuted-source MAE 0.06257521756337783 and zero-response-control MAE 0.21577661527598374 concern interventions on the same package. Constant refers to zeroed target observations in the protocol, not necessarily a constant predictor; permuted refers to independent row-wise circular shifts of source columns. These are sensitivity checks, not isolated ablations or proof of the mechanism, validity, or absence of contamination.

Search and final are different evidence scopes: development uses arc_challenge, ifeval, commonsense, and gsm with seeds 101 and 211; final uses bbh, gpqa, mmlu_pro, musr, openllm_math, legalbench, math, med_qa, and mmlu with seeds 1009, 2003, and 3001. No pooled search/final table, before/after gain, cross-variant significance, search-score delta, or attempt-loss rate is planned. No study.* namespace exists here to support a downstream campaign accounting analysis.

Preserve original-comparator honesty: the initial anchor/ridge implementation is readable under task/program_0 but has no matched final measurements in this bundle; omit a quantitative original-program comparison rather than borrowing an incumbent score from memory. Retain the four actual recorded final comparators. No controlled ablation bundle exists.
figure_plan: Figure 1, early overview: historical source responses and full source scores produce one common score-targeted item path; a new target contributes only queried answers to a source-selected decoder; complete retained target scores are used solely for external evaluation. Distinguish source fitting, legal target observation, and scoring by labeled lanes and a visual information boundary. Mark optional nonlinear decoding as source-selected, not as an experimentally established mechanism.

Figure 2, aggregate paired comparison: a horizontal forest plot of candidate-minus-baseline MAE for the four recorded baselines, using the one supplied aggregate lineage-block interval per comparator and a zero line. A nearby compact table carries absolute errors and separately identified ranking results.

Figure 3, scope and reversals: two vertically stacked dot-plot panels, one with the five leaderboard cases and one with the four HELM cases; within each case show the three budget-specific candidate-minus-local-IRT MAEs using displaced symbols, not connected progression curves. A common signed x-axis exposes local losses as well as gains.
